title: Gangtok on a Budget: What Things Really Cost
meta_description: Indicative 2025–26 Gangtok prices: shared jeeps, Tsomgo seats vs reserved cars, dorms, homestays and momos, plus three daily budgets and common overspends.
summary: Gangtok and East Sikkim cost about ₹1,500–2,500 a person a day on a shoestring, ₹2,500–4,000 at a value level and ₹4,000–6,500 for comfort. Shared jeeps, shared permit-tour seats, dorms and village homestays keep it cheap; reserved cars for every hop and peak-week rooms make it expensive. All prices are indicative for 2025–26.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: Gangtok is not a cheap town in the way a plains town is cheap, but it is a fair one. A bed in a hostel dorm costs ₹500–800, a plate of momos ₹80–150, a cup of tea ₹20–40, and a seat in a shared jeep up from Siliguri ₹350–500. A careful solo traveller can live well here on ₹1,500–2,500 a day, and a couple sharing a modest hotel room can travel comfortably on ₹2,500–4,000 each.

Two things decide your bill more than anything else. The first is how you move: shared jeeps and shared tour seats cost a fraction of a reserved car. The second is when you come: the Puja and Diwali weeks, Christmas to New Year and the May–June school holidays fill rooms and push prices up. Everything below is indicative for 2025–26. Fares, permit fees and tour rates change, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: A price list for 2025–26
paras: These are the numbers we use when friends ask us what to budget. Rooms are per night; everything else is per person unless the line says a car. Homestay rates include dinner and breakfast, which is how almost every village homestay in East Sikkim prices its beds.

sections.heading: Permit tours: per seat or per car
paras: The single biggest spend for most visitors is the high-road day to Tsomgo Lake, Baba Mandir and, for Indian nationals, Nathu La. You cannot simply drive yourself: the permit is arranged through a registered Gangtok tour operator or driver, and the operator either sells you a seat in a shared vehicle or rents you the whole car.

A shared seat for Tsomgo and Baba Mandir runs about ₹800–1,200 a person. A reserved SUV for the same day costs about ₹4,000–5,500, and adding Nathu La takes it to about ₹5,500–7,500 a vehicle. For a solo traveller or a couple the shared seat is the obvious choice. For a family of five or six the reserved car comes out close to the shared price and lets you stop where you like. Ask whether the permit charge is included before you pay, and check current status before you travel, because Nathu La closes to tourists on some weekdays and in bad weather.

The same arithmetic applies on shorter day trips. Rumtek, 24 km away, costs ₹80–150 a seat in a shared taxi from the Lal Bazaar area stand, against ₹1,500–2,500 for a reserved car there and back. The Silk Route is where a reserved vehicle becomes hard to avoid: an SUV with driver costs about ₹5,000–7,000 a day, so it pays to fill it. A cheaper start is a shared jeep from Gangtok to Rongli for ₹200–300 a seat, with your Zuluk or Gnathang homestay arranging the onward vehicle and the permit. Ask your host before you go, because arrangements differ from village to village.

sections.heading: Where to sleep for less
paras: Central Gangtok, around MG Marg and Tibet Road, has the widest range of beds: hostel dorms at ₹500–800, plain budget hotels at ₹1,500–3,000 a double, and mid-range rooms at ₹3,000–5,500. Staying central saves money in a quieter way too, because you can walk to the market, the cafes and the taxi stands instead of paying ₹100–300 for every short hop.

Outside the town, the cheapest good nights are in village homestays. In Zuluk, Gnathang, Padamchen and Aritar a bed with dinner and breakfast costs about ₹1,200–2,200 a person, and the meals are usually the best home cooking of the trip. Rooms are simple, hot water may come in a bucket, and in winter the blankets are heavy for a reason. Book ahead for the Silk Route villages in April–May and October–November, when groups fill them.

Two nights out of town also cut the bill in Gangtok itself. A night at Rumtek or Aritar, where rooms and homestays cost less than central Gangtok in peak weeks, breaks a long trip into cheaper pieces and puts you close to the monastery or the lake at the quiet ends of the day. Pakyong has only a few places to stay, and Rangpo is a transit town, so we would not plan a night in either on purpose.

sections.heading: Eating well on ₹400–600 a day
paras: Food is where Gangtok is kind to a budget. A breakfast of tea and sha phaley or a plate of momos costs ₹100–200, a bowl of thukpa or thenthuk at lunch ₹100–180, and a full thali at dinner ₹150–300. Eat where office workers and drivers eat, in the small canteens off MG Marg and around Lal Bazaar, and ₹400–600 a day covers three proper meals with tea in between.

The cafes on MG Marg itself charge more for the view of the evening crowd, and that is fine for one coffee. Bottled water adds up over a week; most hotels and homestays will fill a bottle with boiled or filtered water if you ask.

Out on the Silk Route and in Aritar, food is folded into the homestay rate, which makes those days the cheapest of the whole trip for eating. Lunch on the road costs ₹100–200 at the tea shops of Zuluk, Kupup or the lakeside at Tsomgo, where noodles, momos and tea are the usual menu. At 3,700–4,300 m eat lightly and drink plenty; it is the altitude, not the price, that should decide how much you order.

sections.heading: Three daily budgets compared
paras: These are per person per day in Gangtok itself, twin sharing where a room is involved, on a day that is not a permit-tour day. Add the tour seat or your share of the car on the day you go up to Tsomgo.

sections.heading: Where people overspend
list: Booking a reserved car for every short hop in town, when the walk from MG Marg to most hotels is ten minutes and a taxi hop costs ₹100–300.
Buying a seven-point sightseeing package that bundles viewpoints you can reach on foot or by a single taxi ride.
Arriving during Durga Puja, Diwali or the New Year week without a booking, and taking the last room at double the usual rate.
Paying for a reserved SUV to Tsomgo as a couple, when a shared seat costs ₹800–1,200 each.
Hiring boots and coats at every stop on the high road instead of carrying one warm layer from home; hire is ₹100–200 a set, and it adds up for a family.
Buying bottled water all week instead of refilling from the hotel.

sections.heading: Money practicalities
paras: Carry cash for the Silk Route and village homestays, where card machines and digital payments may not work if the network drops. In Gangtok most hotels and many cafes take UPI. Keep small notes for taxis, tea stalls and the ropeway counter.

Remember that the rules against littering, spitting and smoking on MG Marg are enforced with fines, which is one unplanned cost you can avoid entirely. And if you plan to go on into North Sikkim or across to Pelling, budget an extra day for road closures: the Teesta valley roads have had long interruptions since the October 2023 flood, so check current status before you travel.

Foreign travellers have one welcome saving: the Restricted Area Permit needed to enter Sikkim is free, issued at the Rangpo check post, at Sikkim Tourism offices including the one at Siliguri SNT, or online. The Protected Area Permit for Tsomgo comes through a registered agent, who builds the charge into the tour price. Indian travellers need no permit to enter Sikkim at all, only for the high places. Check current status before you travel, because the rules and the paperwork change.

faqs.q: How much does a 4-day Gangtok trip cost per person?
faqs.a: On a shoestring, about ₹7,000–9,000 a person from Siliguri and back, using shared jeeps, a dorm or cheap hotel and a shared Tsomgo seat. At a value level, with a budget hotel room shared by two and one reserved sightseeing car, expect ₹11,000–15,000. Peak weeks add a third or more to rooms. These are indicative 2025–26 figures; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is a shared Tsomgo tour cheaper than hiring a car?
faqs.a: For one or two people, yes by a wide margin. A shared seat for Tsomgo and Baba Mandir costs about ₹800–1,200, while a reserved SUV costs about ₹4,000–5,500 for the whole vehicle. For a group of five or six the reserved car comes close to the shared price per head and gives you control of stops. Confirm that the permit is included in the quote.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest way to get from Siliguri to Gangtok?
faqs.a: The SNT bus is the cheapest at about ₹250–350, followed by a shared jeep or taxi seat at ₹350–500 from the SNT stand or the Panitanki More area. The jeep is usually quicker and leaves when full. The road takes 4–5 hours and longer in monsoon, and NH10 has had closures since the October 2023 Teesta flood, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much is a hostel or budget hotel in Gangtok?
faqs.a: A dorm bed in central Gangtok costs about ₹500–800 a night, and a plain double room in a budget hotel about ₹1,500–3,000 off-peak. Mid-range rooms run ₹3,000–5,500. Prices rise during the Puja and Diwali weeks, New Year and the May–June school holidays, when booking ahead matters more than bargaining. All rates are indicative for 2025–26.

faqs.q: How much do momos and thukpa cost in Gangtok?
faqs.a: A plate of momos costs about ₹80–150 in local cafes and canteens, a bowl of thukpa or thenthuk about ₹100–180, and a thali ₹150–300. Tea is ₹20–40 a cup. Cafes on MG Marg charge more than the small places in side lanes and around Lal Bazaar. A budget traveller can eat three good meals a day for ₹400–600.

faqs.q: Do Silk Route homestays include meals?
faqs.a: Almost always. Homestays in Zuluk, Gnathang, Padamchen and Aritar usually quote ₹1,200–2,200 a person with dinner and breakfast, and lunch can be added for a small charge. Meals are home cooked: rice, dal, a vegetable, often chicken or eggs, and local greens. Carry cash, because card and UPI payments depend on a network that can drop in the hills.

faqs.q: How much does a Nathu La trip cost?
faqs.a: A reserved SUV covering Tsomgo, Baba Mandir and Nathu La costs about ₹5,500–7,500 a vehicle in 2025–26, split among up to five or six people. Shared seats including Nathu La are sold on some days. Nathu La is open only to Indian nationals, needs a permit through a registered Gangtok agent and closes to tourists on some weekdays; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Gangtok more expensive than Darjeeling?
faqs.a: Broadly similar for beds and food, slightly higher for transport, because the permit-tour days to Tsomgo and Nathu La must go through registered operators and vehicles. A dorm in Gangtok costs about ₹500–800 and a budget room ₹1,500–3,000, close to Darjeeling rates. The difference shows mostly on the high-road day, where a shared seat keeps it manageable.

faqs.q: When is Gangtok cheapest to visit?
faqs.a: The monsoon months of June to September and the cold weeks of January and February outside the New Year rush usually bring the lowest room rates. Monsoon brings landslides and closed roads, and winter can close Nathu La and the Silk Route with snow, so a cheap room may come with lost days. Check current status before you travel.
